veranderings.voor: Sy is in Graad 6 en hy is in Graad 2.
veranderings.na: Sy was in Graad 6 en hy in Graad 2.
veranderings.rede: The story is told in the past tense, so the present 'is' jars; the repeated verb can also fall away.

veranderings.voor: het Kobus op die gladde modder gegly
veranderings.na: het Kobus op die gladde modder uitgegly
veranderings.rede: 'Uitgly' is the idiomatic Afrikaans verb for slipping and falling; 'gly' alone suggests sliding.

veranderings.voor: In Kobus se klas was 'n nuwe seun
veranderings.na: In Kobus se klas was daar 'n nuwe seun
veranderings.rede: An existential sentence introducing a new character reads more naturally with 'daar'.
'Net' for 'only just' is an English calque; Afrikaans uses 'eers' for a recent point in time.

veranderings.voor: Hy wou die volgende dag vroeër gaan om voor die klok te speel.
veranderings.na: Hy wou die volgende dag vroeër skool toe gaan om te speel voordat die klok lui.
veranderings.rede: 'Vroeër gaan' lacks a destination and 'voor die klok' is elliptical; spelling both out keeps the meaning and reads naturally.

veranderings.na: Daardie aand het Lwazi se ma
veranderings.rede: The new paragraph opens with 'sy' right after a sentence about the old man, so naming her makes the reference clear.
'n Bak van haar pampoensop' copies the English 'a bowl of her soup'; Afrikaans says simply 'n bak pampoensop'.
'Motorhuis' is the standard Afrikaans word; 'garage' is an informal borrowing.

veranderings.voor: Sy knieë was styf en hy moes
veranderings.na: Sy knieë was styf, en hy moes
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: 'en' joins two sentences that each have their own subject and verb, so a comma goes before it.

veranderings.voor: Nadia het omgekyk na die huise langs die veld.
veranderings.na: Nadia het na die huise langs die veld omgekyk.
veranderings.rede: The separable verb belongs at the end of the clause in standard Afrikaans word order.
